input.quote: 7.1 The APCN2 Capital Costs as defined in Paragraph 5 shall be borne by the Parties in the proportions set forth in Schedule B.
input.rationale: Paragraph 7.1/7.2 bind us to bear Capital Costs and O&M Costs in our fixed Schedule B proportions, and Paragraph 12.2 ties Allocated Capacity to that committed financial investment. The commitment runs for the whole twenty-five year Initial Period (18.1), can only be escaped by unanimous agreement or a 90% vote (18.2), and exit forfeits capital already contributed (18.3 chain: \"No credit for capital costs will be made to a Party that terminates its participation\"). There is no right to reduce our share (the only \"no Party shall be forced\" protections in 13.2/14.1 cover future upgrades only) and no shortfall true-up. That is a multi-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination right, i.e. walk-away territory, so it fails the fallback. Deleting the consortium cost-sharing model to reach the preferred position would require collateral rewrites of Schedules B and C, so we target the fallback with a single inserted subparagraph limiting the commitment to the then-current 12-month period, allowing reduction on 30 days' notice and settling shortfall by true-up rather than penalty. We do not re-flag the Paragraph 18 exit terms, which are covered by the term/termination rules.

mappings.element: The commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.
Customer may reduce the commitment on 30 days' notice.
Any shortfall is handled through a true-up rather than a penalty.

proposal.summary: Limit the Schedule B cost-sharing commitment to a rolling 12-month period, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up instead of a penalty.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Paragraph 7 commits us to bear Capital Costs and O&M Costs in our Schedule B proportions for the full twenty-five year Initial Period with no way to reduce that share, which is a multi-year take-or-pay. We have added a short subparagraph limiting the commitment to the then-current twelve month period, allowing reduction on thirty days' notice and settling any shortfall by true-up of actual costs rather than a penalty or forfeiture, which is our fallback position.

ops.text: Each Party's obligation under Subparagraphs 7.1 and 7.2 to bear Capital Costs and O&M Costs in the proportions set forth in Schedule B is limited to the then-current twelve (12) month period, and a Party may reduce those proportions on not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the CBP. Any resulting shortfall shall be settled by a true-up of the costs actually incurred to the effective date of the reduction, and no penalty or forfeiture shall apply.
